definition: To make clear, explain thoroughly, or throw light upon a complex biological mechanism or pathway.
etymology: From Late Latin elucidatus, past participle of elucidare ('to make clear').
manuscriptExample: Further crystallographic studies are required to elucidate the active site geometry of the enzyme.
conferenceExample: The presentation clearly elucidated the feedback loop regulating microRNA expression during hypoxia.

definition: Derived from or verifiable through direct observation or controlled experiment rather than pure theory.
etymology: From Latin empiricus, from Ancient Greek ἐμπειρικός (empeirikós, 'experienced').
manuscriptExample: We provided empirical verification of membrane permeability using fluorescence recovery after photobleaching.
conferenceExample: Theoretical kinetics must be supported by empirical binding affinity assays prior to journal acceptance.

definition: A state of genuine clinical or scientific uncertainty regarding the relative efficacy of competing treatments.
manuscriptExample: Clinical trial enrollment proceeded under strict ethical equipoise between standard-of-care and immunotherapy.
conferenceExample: The IRB committee confirmed that genuine equipoise was maintained throughout the multi-center trial.
